issues.legal_issue: A second appeal under Section 100 of the Code of Civil Procedure cannot be decided without framing and answering a substantial question of law.

Section 20 of the Kerala Land Conservancy Act bars a civil suit only when it concerns an order made under the Act, and does not bar an independent suit to establish title by adverse possession merely because the land is government property.

A claimant seeking title by adverse possession over government land must prove, through clear and cogent evidence, open, continuous, hostile possession accompanied by animus possidendi for the statutory period.
Long-term possession, estimated from the age of trees and unsupported by concrete evidence of hostile possession, is insufficient to establish title by adverse possession over government land.
